original_target.title: Localization of light rays in the planar random mirror model

full_original_statement: Independently at each vertex of $`\mathbb Z^2`$, put no mirror with probability $`1-p`$, a mirror of slope $`+1`$ with probability $`p/2`$, or a mirror of slope $`-1`$ with probability $`p/2`$. A ray moves along nearest-neighbor lattice edges. At each encountered vertex it continues straight if no mirror is present and otherwise undergoes specular reflection through the indicated diagonal mirror. Launch a ray from the origin pointing east, and subsequently apply these rules also on returns to the origin. For every $`p\in(0,1]`$, is the set of visited vertices almost surely finite? Equivalently, must the directed trajectory eventually close into a finite orbit?
